49-[Per90], the Greenberger-Holt-Zeilinger (GHZ) states under Pauli measurements
50-[GHSZ90, GHZ89, Mer90], the Peres-Mermin `magic' square, and the whole class
51-of models admitting All-vs-Nothing (AvN) arguments [ABK+15], there is evi-
52:dence of a significant amount of false positives (e.g. the Hardy model [Har93]).
53-In fact, subsequent work has highlighted many limits of the C ech cohomology
54-approach, including the fact that it does not provide a full invariant for contex-
55-tuality even in its strongest form [Car17], and even under strong assumptions
56-on the measurement scenarios.
57-
--
61-used in measurement based quantum computation (MBQC). However, these
62-methods do not represent a full invariant for contextuality, and they are limited
63-to the class of contextuality arguments relevant for MBQC. Roumen's cohomol-
64-ogy of effect algebras [Rou16], provides an alternative viewpoint, based on cyclic
65-and order cohomology. The author partially addresses the question of existence
66:of false positives, and suggests that order cohomology does not produce any
67:false positives. However, the result is obtained at the expense of the practical
68-computatability of the cohomology invariant, which appears so complex that no
69-application to concrete empirical models has been presented yet.
70-
71-    The aim of this paper is to refine the theory of C ech cohomology in order to
72:obtain a complete invariant which is applicable to the vast majority of empirical
73-models, without compromising the practical computability of the cohomology
74-obstructions.

370-    Note that cohomology only provides a sufficient condition for contextuality,
371:which is not necessary in general. False positives do exist, as we shall see in
372-detail in the following section. The key subtlety that leads to such detection
373-errors is that the vanishing of the cohomology obstruction (s) implies that s is
374-a part of a compatible family for the presheaf F. However this compatible family
375-may not be a valid family for S, because S does not allow linear combinations
376-of sections.

795-4.3 Interpretation and examples
796-
797-At the end of the previous section, we briefly sketched our strategy to avoid
798:false positives, which consists of considering multiple compatible local sections
799:at the same time, instead of focusing on a single one. The notion of joint model
800-
801-         14
802-perfectly embodies this idea. As discussed above, local sections of the first
803:joint model of an empirical model S are pairs of sections of S above adjacent
804-contexts. This allows one to `force' the selection of the sections on adjacent
805-contexts in the original model, thus reducing the chances of the existence of a
806:false positive. Higher-level joint models further refine this approach and allow to
807-consider three, four, k compatible sections at the same time. These statements
808-will be made precise in Section 6, but it is worth giving some examples that will
809-guide us through the technical results.

1499:    The following theorem is the key result of the paper. It shows that, on cyclic
1500-scenarios, all the n-partial families for F (k), where n  k, can be replaced by
1501-a standard form of the same size. In other words, any potential cohomological
1502:false positive of size n  k can be erased. This fact will lead us to a fundamental
1503:result, namely that it is sufficient to take the (|M| - 1)-joint model of a cyclic
1504:scenario to remove every cohomology false positive with certainty (Corollary
1505-7.7).

1703:    This theorem tells us that if we want to study the contextuality of a cyclic
1704-scenario X, M, (Om)m , it is sufficient to analyse the cohomology of its (|M| -
1705:1)-th joint model to assert with certainty which sections give rise to contextual
1706-behavior. This is a major step forward, as this method allows us to get rid of
1707:all the false positives introduced in section 3, and many others, as we shall see
1708-in the rest of the paper.

1871-extended to an extremely vast class of scenarios. This result will lead us to
1872-conjecture that the invariant works universally.
1873-
1874-    Although cyclic models constitute only a fraction of all the possible empirical
1875-models, they play a crucial role in the study of contextuality. Indeed, it was
1876:proven in [Bar15], thanks to an adaptation of Vorob'ev's theorem [Vor62], that
1877-a necessary condition for contextuality is the ciclicity of the measurement cover.
1878-Ciclicity in [Bar15] is a notion coming from database theory, and it is not strictly
1879-equivalent to the one we introduced in this paper. However, it is easy to prove
1880-that any cyclic cover in the sense of [Bar15] must contain at least one cyclic
1881-subcover in the sense defined here. The fact that the existence of cycles in
1882-the cover is necessary for contextuality suggests that contextual features can be
1883-observed by focusing uniquely on the cycles.
1884-
1885:    To convey this idea, we introduce here the notion of cyclic contextuality
1886-property (CCP). The contextual features of models equipped with the CCP can
1887-always be recovered by looking at cycles in the cover M(1).
1888-
1889-        35
1890-Definition 8.1. Let S be an empirical model on a measurement scenario
1891: X, M, (Om)m . We say that S has the cyclic contextuality property (CCP)
1892-if, for each local section s of S such that LC(S, s), there exists a cycle D?  M
1893-for M(1) (called the contextual cycle of s) such that LC(S |D? , s), where S |D?
1894-is the model obtained by restricting S on the subcover D?.
1895-
1896-    Most empirical models satisfy the CCP. To give an idea of how common

1978-    This result shows that, if a model has the CCP, then studying its contex-
1979-tuality is equivalent to study the cohomological contextuality of its (N - 1)-th
1980:joint model. In other words, cohomological contextuality on S(N-1) is a full
1981-invariant for contextuality on the original model. As for cyclic scenarios, note
1982:that it might be possible to erase cohomological false positives for a particular
1983-model even at a lower level.
1984-
1985-    Obviously, we usually do not know a priori whether a model satisfies the
1986-CCP, however, as we mentioned earlier, this property is extremely common
1987-among empirical models, which means that this method is widely applicable.

2314-
2315-9 Conclusions and further directions
2316-
2317:Thanks to the joint model construction, we introduced a cohomology obstruc-
2318:tion to the extension of local sections, which represents a complete invariant for
2319-contextuality in the extremely vast class of models satisfying the cyclic contex-
2320-tuality property. We showed how this invariant gets rid of all the known false
2321-positives from the literature, and proved its efficacy in general models. There
2322-are strong indications suggesting that this cohomology obstruction represents a
2323-full invariant for contextuality in all models. Indeed, in order to give rise to a
2324-
2325-                                 43
2326:false positive, a model S on a scenario X, M, (Om)m would have to satisfy all
2327-of the following:
2328-
2329-    ? S is contextual.
2330-
2331-    ? X, M, (Om)m is non-cyclic.
2332-    ? S does not satisfy the CCP.
2333-
2334:    ? S gives rise to a cohomology false positive in all its joint versions at all
2335-       its sections.
2336-
2337-For this reason, we propose the following conjecture
2338-
2339-Conjecture 9.1. Given a general model S on a scenario X, M, (Om)m , there
2340-exists a k  0 such that
2341-
2342-                                    LC(S, s)  CLC(k)(S, s),
2343-
2344:for all sections s of S. In other words, the cohomology of joint models represents
2345-a full invariant for contextuality.
2346-
2347-    Proving this conjecture will be our main focus in future work.

    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01888v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1701.01888v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We provide a cohomological framework for contextuality of quantum mechanics that is suited to describing contextuality as a resource in measurement-based quantum computation. This framework applies to the parity proofs first discussed by Mermin, as well as a different type of contextuality proofs based on symmetry transformations. The topological arguments presented can be used in the state-dependent and the state-independent case.</summary>

  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:16:                                                 
  to describing contextuality as a resource in measurement-based quantum computation. This

  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:18:

> C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:19:

  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:20:

Introduction
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:22:
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:23:                                           
Contextuality [1]-[5] is a feature that distinguishes quantum mechanics from classical physics. To
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:24:                                           
describe it, let's consider the question of whether it is possible to assign "pre-existing" outcomes
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:25:                                           to 
measurements of quantum observables which are merely revealed by measurement. If this were
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:26:                                           
possible, it would amount to a description of quantum mechanics in terms of classical statistical
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:27:                                           
mechanics. Assuming such a model, for any two different sets A and B of mutually compatible
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:54:for MBQC are generalizations of Mermin's star, 
in the sense that they invoke an algebraic contra-
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:55:diction to the existence of even a single 
non-contextual consistent value assignment. By its intended
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:56:scope, the present framework only needs to apply 
to such kinds of proofs. But then there is an
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:57:additional requirement: the cohomological 
framework in question needs to reproduce the original
> C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:58:parity proofs in a topological guise. The reason 
for this requirement is that both the parity proofs
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:59:and the classical side-processing required in 
every MBQC are based on the same linear relations
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:60:(See Appendix A for a summary on contextuality 
in MBQC; also see [18]).
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:61:
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:62:    Next to the parity-based proofs of 
contextuality exemplified by Mermin's square and star, we
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:63:investigate a different type of contextuality 
proof which is based on symmetry. The central object
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:64:in these proofs is the group of transformations 
that leave the set of observables involved in a
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:65:parity-based contextuality proof invariant, up 
to phases. We show that nontrivial cohomology of
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:66:the symmetry group implies contextuality. 
Furthermore, the parity-based and the symmetry-based
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:67:contextuality proofs are related. Every 
symmetry-based proof implies a parity-based proof.
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:68:
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:69:    To summarize, we examine proofs of 
contextuality of quantum mechanics that have two at-
> C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:70:tributes. They can either be parity-based or 
symmetry-based, and be state-independent or state-
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:71:dependent. There are thus four combinations, and 
for each of these types of proofs we present a
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:72:topological formulation. The parity-based 
contextuality proofs are discussed in Section 4 and the
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:73:symmetry-based proofs in Section 5.
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:74:
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:75:2 First example
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:76:
> C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:77:To illustrate what "reproducing the original

  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:78:
  C:\Users\zwl62\AppData\Local\Temp\automath_a9_lit\1701.01888.txt:79:as a first example Mermin's square [3] (also see

9 Conclusions and further directions

Thanks to the joint model construction, we introduced a cohomology obstruc-
tion to the extension of local sections, which represents a complete invariant for
contextuality in the extremely vast class of models satisfying the cyclic contex-
tuality property. We showed how this invariant gets rid of all the known false
positives from the literature, and proved its efficacy in general models. There
are strong indications suggesting that this cohomology obstruction represents a
full invariant for contextuality in all models. Indeed, in order to give rise to a

                                 43
false positive, a model S on a scenario X, M, (Om)m would have to satisfy all
of the following:

    · S is contextual.

    · X, M, (Om)m is non-cyclic.
    · S does not satisfy the CCP.

    · S gives rise to a cohomology false positive in all its joint versions at all
       its sections.

For this reason, we propose the following conjecture

Conjecture 9.1. Given a general model S on a scenario X, M, (Om)m , there
exists a k  0 such that

                                    LC(S, s)  CLC(k)(S, s),

for all sections s of S. In other words, the cohomology of joint models represents
a full invariant for contextuality.

    Proving this conjecture will be our main focus in future work.

equivalent to the one we introduced in this paper. However, it is easy to prove
that any cyclic cover in the sense of [Bar15] must contain at least one cyclic
subcover in the sense defined here. The fact that the existence of cycles in
the cover is necessary for contextuality suggests that contextual features can be
observed by focusing uniquely on the cycles.

    To convey this idea, we introduce here the notion of cyclic contextuality
property (CCP). The contextual features of models equipped with the CCP can
always be recovered by looking at cycles in the cover M(1).

        35
Definition 8.1. Let S be an empirical model on a measurement scenario
 X, M, (Om)m . We say that S has the cyclic contextuality property (CCP)
if, for each local section s of S such that LC(S, s), there exists a cycle D·  M
for M(1) (called the contextual cycle of s) such that LC(S |D· , s), where S |D·
is the model obtained by restricting S on the subcover D·.

    Most empirical models satisfy the CCP. To give an idea of how common
this property is, it is sufficient to say that all the models that have appeared
in the literature on the sheaf description of contextuality share this property.
For instance, it was proven in [ABCP17] that strong contextuality in quantum
models obtained by applying Pauli measurements to stabiliser states can be
witnessed by only looking at a cycle of size 4.

    Remarkably, the cohomology invariant introduced in the previous sections
can be immediately extended to all models equipped with the CCP.

Proposition 8.2. Let S be a model on a general scenario X, M, (Om)m , and
suppose S has the CCP. For all sections s of S, we have

                                  LC(S, s)  CLC(n-1)(S, s),

where n denotes the size of the contextual cycle of s.

Proof. The implication CLC(n-1)(S, s)  LC(S, s) follows from Theorem 7.2.
Now, suppose LC(S, s). Let D·  M be the contextual cycle of s. By definition,
we have LC(S |D· , s). The model S |D· is defined on the cyclic scenario D·, thus
we can apply Theorem 7.7 to conclude that CLC(n-1)(S |D· , s), which readily
implies CLC(n-1)(S, s).

    Thanks to this simple proposition, we can extend Theorem 7.7 to models
satisfying the CCP over general scenarios. To prove this, we will need the
following proposition

Proposition 8.3. Let S be an empirical model on a scenario X, M, (Om)m .
For all k  0 and every section s of S, we have

                            CLC(k)(S, s)  CLC(l)(S, s) l  k.

Similarly,

            CSC(S(k))  CSC(S(l)) l  k.

Proof. We are going to prove that ¬CLC(k+1)(S, s)  ¬CLC(k)(S, s), and the
result will follow by induction. Suppose ¬CLC(k+1)(S, s). Then there exists a
context C = {C1, C2}  M(k+1) and a section t = (t1, t2)  S(k+1)(C ) (where
t1  S(k)(C1) and t2  S(k)(C2)) such that s  flatten(t) and ¬CLC(S(k+1), t).

In particular, this means that there exists a compatible family

tuality is equivalent to study the cohomological contextuality of its (N - 1)-th
joint model. In other words, cohomological contextuality on S(N-1) is a full
invariant for contextuality on the original model. As for cyclic scenarios, note
that it might be possible to erase cohomological false positives for a particular
model even at a lower level.

    Obviously, we usually do not know a priori whether a model satisfies the
CCP, however, as we mentioned earlier, this property is extremely common
among empirical models, which means that this method is widely applicable.
In the following section we will give some examples to support this claim.

ID: 2204.06648
TITLE: Simplicial quantum contextuality
LEAD: Cihan Okay
DOI: 10.22331/q-2023-05-22-1009
ABSTRACT: We introduce a new framework for contextuality based on simplicial sets, combinatorial models of topological spaces that play a prominent role in modern homotopy theory. Our approach extends measurement scenarios to consist of spaces (rather than sets) of measurements and outcomes, and thereby generalizes nonsignaling distributions to simplicial distributions, which are distributions on spaces modeled by simplicial sets. Using this formalism we present a topologically inspired new proof of Fine's theorem for characterizing noncontextuality in Bell scenarios. Strong contextuality is generalized suitably for simplicial distributions, allowing us to define cohomological witnesses that extend the earlier topological constructions restricted to algebraic relations among quantum observables to the level of probability distributions. Foundational theorems of quantum theory such as the Gleason's theorem and Kochen-Specker theorem can be expressed naturally within this new language.

ID: 2211.00571
TITLE: Simplicial distributions, convex categories and contextuality
LEAD: Aziz Kharoof
DOI: none
ABSTRACT: The data of a physical experiment can be represented as a presheaf of probability distributions. A striking feature of quantum theory is that those probability distributions obtained in quantum mechanical experiments do not always admit a joint probability distribution, a celebrated observation due to Bell. Such distributions are called contextual. Simplicial distributions are combinatorial models that extend presheaves of probability distributions by elevating sets of measurements and outcomes to spaces. Contextuality can be defined in this generalized setting. This paper introduces the notion of convex categories to study simplicial distributions from a categorical perspective. Simplicial distributions can be given the structure of a convex monoid, a convex category with a single object, when the outcome space has the structure of a group. We describe contextuality as a monoid-theoretic notion by introducing a weak version of invertibility for monoids. Our main result is that a simplicial distribution is noncontextual if and only if it is weakly invertible. Similarly, strong contextuality and contextual fraction can be characterized in terms of invertibility in monoids. Finally, we show that simplicial homotopy can be used to detect extremal simplicial distributions refining the earlier methods based on Cech cohomology and the cohomology of groups.

ID: 2310.18135
TITLE: Equivariant simplicial distributions and quantum contextuality
LEAD: Cihan Okay
DOI: none
ABSTRACT: We introduce an equivariant version of contextuality with respect to a symmetry group, which comes with natural applications to quantum theory. In the equivariant setting, we construct cohomology classes that can detect contextuality. This framework is motivated by the earlier topological approach to contextuality producing cohomology classes that serve as computational primitives in measurement-based quantum computing.

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

\section{Boundary with empirical-model obstructions}
\label{sec:empirical-boundary}

Let \(X\) be a finite set of measurements, let \(O_x\) be a finite nonempty
outcome set for each \(x\in X\), and let \(\mathcal M\) be a finite antichain
of contexts covering \(X\).  For a finite empirical model \(e\), write
\[
 S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
\]
for its support presheaf on the downward-closed context category.  Adjoin a
terminal object \(X\), declare \(\mathcal M\) to cover it, and set
\[
 \widehat S_e(X)=\varprojlim_{U}S_e(U).
\]
Thus \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is the set of compatible supported local
assignments.  Let \(aS_e\) be the associated sheaf on this terminally
augmented context site.

\subsection*{The terminal augmentation}

On the original downward-closed context category, a global assignment is a
compatible family rather than a section over a named terminal context,
because the full measurement set \(X\) need not belong to the measurement
cover.  The augmentation adjoins \(X\) as a bookkeeping object and declares
the maximal contexts to cover it.  Its value is
\[
 \widehat S_e(X)
 =\left\{(s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}:
 \begin{array}{l}
 s_C\in S_e(C),\\
 s_C|_{C\cap D}=s_D|_{C\cap D}
 \text{ for all }C,D
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]

Because the event sheaf has unique gluing, a compatible family determines a
unique outcome assignment \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) whose restriction to
each \(C\) is \(s_C\).  Conversely, any assignment whose restriction lies
in every specified support gives such a family.  Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:contextual-global-set}
 \widehat S_e(X)
 \cong
 \left\{s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x:
 s|_C\in S_e(C)\ \text{for all }C\in\mathcal M\right\}.
\end{equation}

The plus construction for the cover \(\mathcal M\to X\) produces the same
set.  All members of a matching family agree strictly on intersections, and
the event sheaf supplies their unique outcome assignment.  Thus
\[
 (aS_e)(X)\cong\widehat S_e(X).
\]
Strong contextuality therefore gives an empty set of global component
sections in the canonical support construction, not a nonempty set of
components carrying non-neutral gerbes.

\begin{theorem}[Empirical-model boundary]
\label{thm:empirical-model-boundary}
For every finite empirical model \(e\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item compatible supported families, globally supported assignments, global
      sections in the Abramsky--Brandenburger sense, and elements of
      \(\widehat S_e(X)\cong(aS_e)(X)\) are naturally the same set.  Hence
      strong contextuality is absence of a matching family at this
      set-valued level, not matching without amalgamation;
\item for every supplied abelian sheaf \(\mathscr A\),
      \[
      \operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\mathscr A
      \]
      is a canonical split \(\mathscr A\)-banded stack lift of \(aS_e\),
      and every one of its component gerbes is neutral;
\item the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction attached to
      \(s\in S_e(C_0)\) is a relative class
      \[
      \gamma_e(s)\in
      \check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}),
      \]
      equivalently a torsor class.  It is not the Giraud \(H^2\)-class of a
      component gerbe.  There can be no construction recovering all such
      classes from a component-section map with component sheaf \(aS_e\):
      for a strongly contextual model the latter map has empty domain
      \((aS_e)(X)=\varnothing\), whereas the AMB classes remain indexed by
      local sections;
\item the homological images and the two-component criterion of
      \Cref{thm:wedge-sphere-two-component-label-loss} apply to an empirical
      model only after a band and a non-split banded prestack lift have been
      supplied as additional data.  They are not invariants of a bare
      empirical model.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The event presheaf
\(\mathcal E(U)=\prod_{x\in U}O_x\) is a sheaf.  A compatible family
\((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\), with \(s_C\in S_e(C)\), therefore glues
uniquely to an assignment \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\), and its restrictions
lie in the stated supports.  Conversely, restricting such an assignment
gives the compatible family.  The terminal right Kan extension is the same
limit by definition, and the plus construction on the cover
\(\mathcal M\to X\) gives the same set in \((aS_e)(X)\).  This proves (i)
and agrees with the standard support formulation of contextuality
\cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}.

The four descriptions in (i) fit into a commutative square:
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
\{\text{compatible support families}\}
 &\longrightarrow&
\{\text{outcome assignments locally in the support}\}\\
\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow\\
\widehat S_e(X)&\longrightarrow&(aS_e)(X).
\end{array}
\]
The upper arrow is unique gluing in \(\mathcal E\), the left arrow is the
definition of the inverse limit, and the lower arrow is the plus-construction
map.  Every arrow is a bijection.  No groupoid or band enters this set-level
statement.

The discrete-groupoid functor sends a sheaf of sets to a stack with that
component sheaf and zero automorphism sheaves.  The classifying stack
\(\mathsf B\mathscr A\) has one component and automorphism sheaf
\(\mathscr A\).  Their product is therefore a split banded lift of
\(aS_e\).  In each component, the identity \(\mathscr A\)-torsor is a
global object, so the component gerbe is neutral and its Giraud class is
zero.  This proves (ii).

Objectwise, the product stack has objects
\[
 (s,T),
 \qquad
 s\in(aS_e)(U),\quad
 T\text{ an }\mathscr A|_U\text{-torsor}.
\]
Two objects can be isomorphic only when their first coordinates agree.
Consequently the component sheaf is \(aS_e\).  The automorphism sheaf of
\((s,T)\) is canonically \(\mathscr A|_U\).  For a global component
section \(s\), the object
\[
 (s,\mathscr A)
\]
with the trivial torsor lies globally in the corresponding full component.
This identifies the neutralizing object directly.

Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa apply the free-abelian presheaf
\(\mathcal F_e=\mathbb Z[S_e]\) and a relative kernel presheaf to obtain
the displayed degree-one Cech class
\cite[Sec.~4]{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}.  Car\`u identifies this
class with an appropriate torsor trivialized by the measurement cover
\cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}.  By contrast, the map in
\Cref{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package} is indexed by global sections
of the component sheaf and takes values in derived \(H^2\) of a sheaf band.
If \(e\) is strongly contextual, (i) gives
\((aS_e)(X)=\varnothing\), so every such component-section map has empty
domain.  Local sections \(s\in S_e(C_0)\) can still exist and index AMB
classes.  This degree and indexing mismatch proves (iii).

The mismatch has two independent parts:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 &\text{AMB obstruction}&\text{component-gerbe obstruction}\\ \hline
\text{index}&s\in S_e(C_0)&v\in(aS_e)(X)\\
\text{degree}&\check H^1&H^2\\
\text{object}&\text{relative torsor}&\text{banded gerbe}\\
\text{canonical lift}&\text{relative kernel data}&\text{split stack.}
\end{array}
\]
Changing degree by a formal shift would not repair the indexing difference.
In a strongly contextual model the right-hand index set is empty, while the
left-hand index set can contain many local sections.  When a global support
assignment does exist, the canonical component indexed by it is neutral.
A nonzero degree-two class requires additional lift data in either case.

Finally, the canonical lift in (ii) has zero component classes and zero
homological image subgroups.  A non-split lift, a finite good-cover nerve,
and prescribed maps \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\) are additional inputs to
\Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}; none is selected by the
support presheaf of a bare empirical model.  This proves (iv).
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}

The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
formulates it for commutative partial monoids
\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.

On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
\(s_0\),
\[
 \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 [\beta_{s_0}]=0
\]
\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.

Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
therefore does not repair the detection problem.

Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
supplied.

The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
not by itself supply the missing class.

\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
models.  If an assignment
\[
 e\longmapsto
 \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
\]
is natural under those isomorphisms, then
\[
 \Theta(e)\in
 H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
\]
Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Additional data required for the finite-site construction}

To apply the prescribed-realization theorem to an empirical model, one would
have to supply, at minimum:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item a finite intersection site with connected nonempty overlaps and a
      connected nerve;
\item a finite abelian band \(A\);
\item an \(A\)-banded prestack whose component presheaf is related to the
      chosen support data;
\item normalized Cech \(2\)-cocycles, or prescribed maps
      \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\), for its component labels;
\item the terminal-fibre behavior required by the comparison criterion.
\end{enumerate}
The support presheaf supplies none of (ii)--(iv).  It supplies a canonical
answer only after one chooses the split product stack, and that answer sets
every degree-two component class to zero.  No construction established here
maps bare support presheaves to the non-split data used by the wedge
corollary.

The exact diagnosis is underdetermination whenever nonzero classes exist and
actual absence only when the relevant \(H^2\) vanishes.  In the former case,
the support presheaf does not determine a preferred nonzero class among the
possible classes; in the latter, no nonzero constant-band class of this type
exists.  Item~(iv) is the decisive missing input, and the non-split part of
item~(iii) is the same obstruction in categorical form.  Indeed,
\Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction} starts from prescribed maps
\(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\) and constructs a prestack realizing them.  It does
not extract those maps from the support presheaf.

One may postulate such lift data for a particular empirical model and then
apply the article's theorems conditionally.  The resulting homological images
belong to that supplied finite presentation and lift, not to the empirical
model alone.  The distinction is the same as in the opening interface: the
paper begins after the site, band, and prestack have been specified.

The theorem concerns possibilistic support.  Probabilistic
noncontextuality asks for a distribution on the global assignment set with
the given marginals, a different extension problem which is not determined
by \(S_e\).  This distinction is independent of the degree mismatch above.

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

"""Finite and symbolic checks for the claims in oracle_sprint_A9_r1.md.

These checks verify only the algebraic consequences of UCT naturality and
NWW's displayed Cechization formula.  They do not prove either open
crossed-module comparison in NWW, Problems 8.1(b) and 8.2.
"""

import argparse
import sys
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from fractions import Fraction
from functools import reduce
from io import StringIO
from itertools import combinations, product
from math import gcd
from pathlib import Path


def _continuous_three_cocycle(a, b, c):
    """A normalized continuous inhomogeneous 3-cocycle on (R,+)."""

    return a * b * c


def _group_coboundary(w, x, y, z):
    f = _continuous_three_cocycle
    return (
        f(x, y, z)
        - f(w + x, y, z)
        + f(w, x + y, z)
        - f(w, x, y + z)
        + f(w, x, y)
    )


def _tau(g, h, k, x):
    f = _continuous_three_cocycle
    return (
        f(h, k - h, x - k)
        - f(g, k - g, x - k)
        + f(g, h - g, x - h)
    )


def _tau_rewrite(g, h, k, x):
    f = _continuous_three_cocycle
    return f(g, h - g, k - h) + f(h - g, k - h, x - k)


def check_real_cechization_identities():
    values = tuple(Fraction(i, 2) for i in range(-4, 5))
    group_cases = 0
    tau_cases = 0
    cech_cases = 0

    for w, x, y, z in product(values, repeat=4):
        assert _group_coboundary(w, x, y, z) == 0
        group_cases += 1

    for g, h, k, x in product(values, repeat=4):
        assert _tau(g, h, k, x) == _tau_rewrite(g, h, k, x)
        tau_cases += 1

    for g, h, k, ell, x in product(values, repeat=5):
        cech_delta = (
            _tau(h, k, ell, x)
            - _tau(g, k, ell, x)
            + _tau(g, h, ell, x)
            - _tau(g, h, k, x)
        )
        assert cech_delta == 0
        cech_cases += 1

    return {
        "group_cocycle_cases": group_cases,
        "tau_rewrite_cases": tau_cases,
        "cech_cocycle_cases": cech_cases,
    }


def _divisors(n):
    return tuple(d for d in range(1, n + 1) if n % d == 0)


def _cyclic_subgroup(n, generators):
    divisor = reduce(gcd, generators, n)
    return frozenset(range(0, n, divisor))


def check_finite_quotient_claims(max_modulus=36):
    factorization_cases = 0
    exact_sequence_cases = 0

    for n in range(1, max_modulus + 1):
        subgroups = tuple(_cyclic_subgroup(n, (d,)) for d in _divisors(n))

        for subgroup in subgroups:
            for quotient_modulus in _divisors(n):
                units = tuple(
                    u for u in range(quotient_modulus) if gcd(u, quotient_modulus) == 1
                ) or (0,)
                for unit in units:
                    kills_image = all((unit * x) % quotient_modulus == 0 for x in subgroup)
                    factors_through = subgroup <= frozenset(
                        x
                        for x in range(n)
                        if (unit * x) % quotient_modulus == 0
                    )
                    pushed_evaluation_is_zero = kills_image
                    assert kills_image == factors_through == pushed_evaluation_is_zero
                    factorization_cases += 1

        for first, second, third in product(subgroups, repeat=3):
            intersection = first & second & third
            subgroup_sum = _cyclic_subgroup(n, tuple(first | second | third))
            assert intersection <= subgroup_sum

            labelled_quotient_order = n // len(intersection)
            common_quotient_order = n // len(subgroup_sum)
            kernel_order = len(subgroup_sum) // len(intersection)
            assert labelled_quotient_order == kernel_order * common_quotient_order
            exact_sequence_cases += 1

    return {
        "factorization_cases": factorization_cases,
        "exact_sequence_cases": exact_sequence_cases,
    }


def _elements(moduli):
    return tuple(product(*(range(modulus) for modulus in moduli)))


def _add(left, right, moduli):
    return tuple((x + y) % modulus for x, y, modulus in zip(left, right, moduli))


def _generated_subgroup(moduli, generators):
    zero = tuple(0 for _ in moduli)
    generated = {zero}
    frontier = [zero]
    while frontier:
        current = frontier.pop()
        for generator in generators:
            candidate = _add(current, generator, moduli)
            if candidate not in generated:
                generated.add(candidate)
                frontier.append(candidate)
    return frozenset(generated)


def _all_subgroups(moduli):
    elements = _elements(moduli)
    zero = tuple(0 for _ in moduli)
    subgroups = []
    for size in range(1, len(elements) + 1):
        for subset_tuple in combinations(elements, size):
            subset = frozenset(subset_tuple)
            if zero not in subset:
                continue
            if all(_add(x, y, moduli) in subset for x in subset for y in subset):
                subgroups.append(subset)
    return tuple(subgroups)


def _minimum_generator_number(moduli, subgroup):
    elements = tuple(subgroup)
    for beta in range(len(elements) + 1):
        if any(
            _generated_subgroup(moduli, generators) == subgroup
            for generators in product(elements, repeat=beta)
        ):
            return beta
    raise AssertionError("finite subgroup has no finite generating tuple")


def check_generator_bound_classification():
    moduli_list = ((2,), (3,), (4,), (2, 2), (2, 3), (2, 2, 2), (2, 4))
    classification_cases = 0

    for moduli in moduli_list:
        elements = _elements(moduli)
        subgroups = _all_subgroups(moduli)
        minimum_generators = {
            subgroup: _minimum_generator_number(moduli, subgroup)
            for subgroup in subgroups
        }

        for beta in range(4):
            homomorphism_images = {
                _generated_subgroup(moduli, generators)
                for generators in product(elements, repeat=beta)
            }
            bounded_generator_subgroups = {
                subgroup
                for subgroup, number in minimum_generators.items()
                if number <= beta
            }
            assert homomorphism_images == bounded_generator_subgroups
            classification_cases += len(subgroups)

    return {"groups": len(moduli_list), "classification_cases": classification_cases}


def pullback_strict_inclusion_example():
    # ev: H_r(S^r v S^r) = Z^2 -> Z/2 is projection to the first factor.
    ambient_image = frozenset({0, 1})
    # Pull back along the inclusion of the second sphere: t |-> (0,t).
    pullback_image = frozenset({0})
    assert pullback_image < ambient_image
    return {
        "ambient_image": ambient_image,
        "pullback_image": pullback_image,
        "ambient_quotient_order": 2 // len(ambient_image),
        "pullback_quotient_order": 2 // len(pullback_image),
    }


def action_lift_peiffer_counterexample():
    # G = K = C_2 and K-hat = C_2 x C_2 with boundary (a,b) |-> a.
    def boundary(element):
        return element[0]

    def action(group_element, element):
        a, b = element
        return (a, (b + group_element * a) % 2)

    def multiply(left, right):
        return ((left[0] + right[0]) % 2, (left[1] + right[1]) % 2)

    def inverse(element):
        return element  # Every element of C_2 x C_2 has order at most two.

    elements = tuple(product(range(2), repeat=2))
    covers_conjugation = all(
        boundary(action(g, element)) == boundary(element)
        for g in range(2)
        for element in elements
    )
    fixes_central_kernel = all(
        action(g, (0, z)) == (0, z) for g in range(2) for z in range(2)
    )
    peiffer_identity = all(
        action(boundary(left), right)
        == multiply(multiply(left, right), inverse(left))
        for left in elements
        for right in elements
    )
    assert covers_conjugation and fixes_central_kernel and not peiffer_identity
    return {
        "covers_conjugation": covers_conjugation,
        "fixes_central_kernel": fixes_central_kernel,
        "peiffer_identity": peiffer_identity,
    }


def _run_verification():
    real = check_real_cechization_identities()
    finite = check_finite_quotient_claims()
    generators = check_generator_bound_classification()
    pullback = pullback_strict_inclusion_example()
    peiffer = action_lift_peiffer_counterexample()
    print("PASS NWW Cechization formula checks:", real)
    print("PASS finite quotient checks:", finite)
    print("PASS generator-bound checks:", generators)
    print("PASS pullback direction check:", pullback)
    print("COUNTEREXAMPLE action lift does not imply Peiffer identity:", peiffer)
    print("OPEN comparisons intentionally unverified: NWW Problems 8.1(b), 8.2(a), 8.2(b)")


def main(argv=()):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.output is None:
        _run_verification()
        return

    capture = StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(capture):
        _run_verification()
    report = capture.getvalue()
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+
