+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.

+not by itself supply the missing class.

+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence â‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter â‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion â‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
âœ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
âŒ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
âœ… Write â†’ Run (pass) â†’ Revert fix â†’ Run (MUST FAIL) â†’ Restore â†’ Run (pass)
âŒ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
âœ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
âŒ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
âœ… Re-read plan â†’ Create checklist â†’ Verify each â†’ Report gaps or completion
âŒ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
âœ… Agent reports success â†’ Check VCS diff â†’ Verify changes â†’ Report actual state
âŒ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion â†’ redirect â†’ rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established
+enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the
+realization theorem of this article begins only after a class has been
+supplied.
+
+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}
+

**Completeness Correction**

The old manuscript did not explicitly claim that AMB was complete, but it said only:

> A bare empirical model has a canonical split stack lift whose component gerbes are neutral.

and the old conclusion said:

> Bare empirical models provide only the support presheaf and its canonical split stack, whose component gerbes are neutral. Their relative degree-one obstructions are indexed differently and are not recovered by the component-section map. A non-split banded lift must therefore be supplied before the finite-site results apply.

That omission could leave the wrong impression that degree one already exhausted the detection question. The introduction, boundary, and conclusion now state explicitly that:

- AMB is sufficient, not complete, for possibilistic contextuality.
- Hardy-type failures exist.
- Carù constructed a strongly contextual counterexample despite substantial symmetry and connectedness.
- Carù’s joint-model invariant is complete for models satisfying the cyclic contextuality property.
- A different degree-two separation is logically possible.
- This manuscript lacks the source-side operation \(e\mapsto\Theta(e)\); it does not prove that no such operation can exist.
- Support data underdetermine a preferred nonzero class when nonzero classes exist; the class is genuinely absent only when the relevant \(H^2\) vanishes.
- Item (iv) is the decisive obstacle, and the non-split part of item (iii) is the same missing datum categorically.
- Theorem 4.2 consumes prescribed maps \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\) and realizes them; it does not extract those maps.

The abstract’s negative transfer statement, every pre-existing numbered result, and the gerbe-classification priority objection were preserved. Theorem 7.1 is unchanged; the new proposition is numbered 7.2.

+\subsection*{Known degree-two obstructions and the remaining boundary}
+
+The degree-two direction in contextuality is not unexplored.  For
+operator-realized parity models, multiplication of compatible observables up
+to phases defines a normalized \(2\)-cocycle.  Rephasing the chosen
+representatives changes that cocycle by a coboundary, and a nonzero class
+obstructs a noncontextual value assignment; in particular, Okay, Roberts,
+Bartlett, and Raussendorf give an \(H^2\)-criterion for state-independent
+contextuality \cite[Thm.~1]{OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017}.  The same
+source-side structure can be expressed through extension data, and Aasn{\ae}ss
+formulates it for commutative partial monoids
+\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Aasnaess2022}.  Simplicial formulations also produce
+degree-two witnesses for strong contextuality
+\cite[Cor.~5.7]{OkayKharoofIpek2023}.  Thus parity proofs, operator phase
+cocycles, central-extension or partial-algebraic presentations, and
+simplicial models already supply degree-two contextuality obstructions.  The
+operator multiplication and phase data used in the first constructions are
+not determined by the possibilistic support, while the simplicial
+construction is a separate source-side theory not contained in this article.
+
+On the overlap with the AMB construction, the known operator-phase
+obstruction is not stronger.  In Aasn{\ae}ss's notation, for a local section
+\(s_0\),
+\[
+ \gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0
+ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ [\beta_{s_0}]=0
+\]
+\cite[Thm.~4.1]{Aasnaess2022}.  Equivalently, a nonzero phase class forces
+the corresponding AMB class to be nonzero.  Hence this degree-two class
+cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.  This comparison concerns
+the algebraically structured common domain; it is not a claim that every
+possible degree-two obstruction is subsumed by AMB.
+
+Nor is the original AMB obstruction complete for possibilistic
+contextuality.  It is a sufficient obstruction, with false positives already
+in Hardy-type examples.  Car\`u gives a strongly contextual model on a simple
+Bell-type scenario for which the standard obstruction vanishes despite
+substantial symmetry and connectedness assumptions
+\cite[Sec.~4]{Caru2017}.  His later joint-model construction removes the known
+false positives and is complete for models satisfying the cyclic
+contextuality property \cite[Thm.~8.4]{Caru2018}.  A direct attempt to continue
+the Cech construction to higher AMB-style obstructions was also made in
+\cite[Sec.~5]{Caru2017}: the natural hierarchy occurs only in higher odd
+degrees, and the higher levels vanish for no-signalling empirical models
+beyond the original degree-one level \cite[Prop.~5.6]{Caru2017}.  That hierarchy
+therefore does not repair the detection problem.
+
+Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual
+model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is
+incomplete.  What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare
+empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle.  The established

+The following elementary observation records why automorphism symmetry does
+not by itself supply the missing class.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Equivariant no-selection]
+\label{prop:equivariant-no-selection}
+Suppose that coefficient groups \(A_e\) and the cohomology groups
+\(H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)\) are functorial under isomorphisms of empirical
+models.  If an assignment
+\[
+ e\longmapsto
+ \Theta(e)\in H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)
+\]
+is natural under those isomorphisms, then
+\[
+ \Theta(e)\in
+ H^2(N(\mathcal M_e);A_e)^{\operatorname{Aut}(e)}.
+\]
+Consequently, if this invariant subgroup is zero, every such natural
+degree-two obstruction vanishes on \(e\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For every \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(e)\), naturality gives
+\(g_*\Theta(e)=\Theta(e)\).  Thus \(\Theta(e)\) is fixed by every automorphism,
+and it is zero when the fixed subgroup is zero.
+\end{proof}

**Boundary Text**

The complete repaired boundary section, verbatim and including the unchanged Empirical-model boundary theorem 7.1, is [sec_branch_contextuality.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_homological_visibility_gluing_obstructions_state_forcing_apal/sec_branch_contextuality.tex:1). The file is 302 lines; reproducing it here would duplicate the authoritative source. The newly added literature repair begins at line 180, proposition 7.2 begins at line 239, and the underdetermination/absence diagnosis begins at line 283.

Its central conclusion now reads verbatim:

> Consequently, a degree-two obstruction separating an AMB-blind contextual  
> model is logically possible, because the degree-one obstruction is  
> incomplete. What is absent here is a construction that consumes bare  
> empirical-model data and produces such a \(2\)-cocycle. The established  
> enriched phase construction does not give the missing separation, and the

The repair records that operator/parity phase cocycles, extension or partial-algebraic formulations, and simplicial models already provide degree-two contextuality obstructions. It then states Aasnæss’s comparison in the required direction:
\[
\gamma(1\mathbin{\cdot}s_0)=0\Longrightarrow[\beta_{s_0}]=0,
\]
so the known operator-phase \(H^2\) class cannot be nonzero on an AMB-blind local section.

It also records Carù’s higher odd-degree hierarchy and its vanishing beyond the original level on no-signalling empirical models. The most natural enriched degree-two crossing is therefore already known and does not supply the missing separation.

**Completeness Correction**

The old manuscript did not explicitly claim that AMB was complete, but it said only:

> A bare empirical model has a canonical split stack lift whose component gerbes are neutral.

and the old conclusion said:

> Bare empirical models provide only the support presheaf and its canonical split stack, whose component gerbes are neutral. Their relative degree-one obstructions are indexed differently and are not recovered by the component-section map. A non-split banded lift must therefore be supplied before the finite-site results apply.

That omission could leave the wrong impression that degree one already exhausted the detection question. The introduction, boundary, and conclusion now state explicitly that:

- AMB is sufficient, not complete, for possibilistic contextuality.
- Hardy-type failures exist.
- Carù constructed a strongly contextual counterexample despite substantial symmetry and connectedness.
- Carù’s joint-model invariant is complete for models satisfying the cyclic contextuality property.
- A different degree-two separation is logically possible.
- This manuscript lacks the source-side operation \(e\mapsto\Theta(e)\); it does not prove that no such operation can exist.
- Support data underdetermine a preferred nonzero class when nonzero classes exist; the class is genuinely absent only when the relevant \(H^2\) vanishes.
- Item (iv) is the decisive obstacle, and the non-split part of item (iii) is the same missing datum categorically.
- Theorem 4.2 consumes prescribed maps \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\) and realizes them; it does not extract those maps.

The abstract’s negative transfer statement, every pre-existing numbered result, and the gerbe-classification priority objection were preserved. Theorem 7.1 is unchanged; the new proposition is numbered 7.2.
